# Zain Dana Harper: tools in plain terms

> Ten tools by Zain Dana Harper, each as a short record: what it does, who it is
> for, how to try it, what it does not do, its current version and licence, and
> where to read more. Versions are current as of 2026-10-23. The short index is
> https://harperz9.github.io/llms.txt and the full product registry, with dated
> evidence for each claim, is https://harperz9.github.io/system/systems.json.

Every tool below runs on your own computer. None needs an account with the
author. Source for each is on GitHub under https://github.com/HarperZ9.

## Flywheel

Version 2.1.0. Licence MIT (OSI-approved; relicensed from MIT via flywheel #574). Python 3.11 or newer, no third-party
runtime dependencies.

- What it is: an AI workstation and coding harness that you host yourself,
  with a desktop app, an assistant (Rowan), a coding agent that works in your
  own folders with your permission, and connected tools for research, memory
  and writing.
- What it does: runs AI tasks on any hosted or local model behind one
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint on your machine, checks the values in an answer
  against the source that decides them (a tax table, a formulary, a court
  calendar, a script you supply), and records every step on a hash-chained
  ledger that can be checked again later, offline.
- Who it is for: developers and teams who use AI agents or model output and
  need to show which parts of an answer were checked, and against what.
- Try it: `python -m pip install flywheel-verify` then `flywheel gate`.
  `flywheel code` runs a coding agent in your terminal.
- What it does not do: it does not decide that an answer is true beyond the
  sources you give it. It reports which fields agree, which disagree, and which
  nothing could confirm. By default the coding agent asks before it writes or
  runs anything.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/flywheel.html ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/flywheel , https://pypi.org/project/flywheel-verify/ ,
  docs https://harperz9.github.io/flywheel/docs/
- Recent verified milestones (2026-11-26): flywheel #565 added the unified
  `flywheel super-solver` pipeline (6/6 adversarial fault catch, 0 silent
  accepts); flywheel #566 added Execution-Oracle PUCT verification tree search
  and a 34.99x RFC 6962 proof-carrying Merkle trace compressor (0 soundness loss);
  flywheel #568 shipped full-track 4096-pt Hann Welch PSD, spectral tilt, macro
  DR, and <120 Hz phase verification in audio_deconstruct.py; flywheel #570
  published Official MCP Registry manifests plus codemeta.json/llms.txt/CITATION.cff;
  flywheel #571 added the C11/Win32 native desktop surface, BuildLang FFI, and
  operator workflows in accountable-surface; flywheel #572 shipped OS keystore
  (Win32 DPAPI/CredMan), OAuth 2.0 PKCE/Device Flow, and RFC 9421 request
  signing; flywheel #573 shipped AgentWorkspace, DelegatedMandate,
  ApprovalValve, and MCP workspace tools; flywheel #574 relicensed Flywheel
  and its consolidated packages to the pure OSI MIT License;
  flywheel #577 (1faa3deb) shipped the `fsp` TPM Stage L/F fail-safe governance
  protocol (180/180 tests, 29/29 red-team attacks caught, #68522);
  Data Forge shipped proof-carrying distillation (283,687.3 rows/s native
  BuildLang = 158.2x Python 1,792.8 rows/s, bit-exact FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 + RFC
  6962 Merkle, 6/6 native + 9/9 pipeline controls); Articulate native BuildLang
  reached 27,606.0 docs/s (4.19e-13 cadence parity, 6/6 traps); INV-01
  Symplectic Loom-Titan-1M reached 194.59 M loops/s native BuildLang (2.22e-16
  parity vs C++23 AVX2+FMA, 0.0812 ms 1M-token PLATO/NSA + MoltKV query, 5/5
  controls); JFC3P-14B-Oracle v5 reached 66/84 Arm C (78.57%, +21.43 pp vs Base
  14B 48/84, 15/15 long-context zero drift, 21/24 traps, 6/6 A1..A6 PASS, live
  HF Space https://huggingface.co/spaces/zaindanaharper/jfc3p-oracle-demo); and
  JFC3P-Titan-1M v2 verified 10.331 GB RTX 4090 / 5.747 GB Edge at 1,000,000
  tokens (291.69x KV compression, 99.85 tok/s). Live 16-receipt SHA-256 ledger:
  https://harperz9.github.io/experiments/#receipt-ledger .

## Articulate

Version 0.19.1. Licence MIT (OSI-approved; relicensed from MIT). Python 3.9 or newer, standard library only.

- What it does: checks prose on your computer and names each writing pattern it
  finds and the line it sits on: stacked hedges, marketing words, corporate
  verbs, contrast framing, rule-of-three lists, em dashes. A profile for each
  kind of writing (procedure, commit, readme, research, essay, narrative)
  decides which findings block.
- Who it is for: anyone who writes documentation, READMEs, release notes,
  essays or commit messages and wants a style check in a terminal, an editor
  (LSP), CI (SARIF) or an AI agent (MCP).
- Try it: `python -m pip install articulate-writing` then
  `articulate check README.md --profile readme --gate`.
- What it does not do: it checks writing style only and makes no claim about
  authorship. On 183 texts of known origin it flagged all 84 AI texts and 57 of
  75 human texts (76%, 95% interval 65% to 84%). It needs no model, account or
  API key.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/articulate.html ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/articulate , https://pypi.org/project/articulate-writing/

## CMMNS

Formerly Daylight Commons, and Radar before that; spoken "commons".
Version 3.11.0. Licence AGPL-3.0-only. A browser extension for Chrome, Edge,
Brave and Firefox 128 or later, plus a command line for saved threads.

- What it does: rest the pointer on a reply on X, YouTube, Reddit, Facebook,
  Instagram, Bluesky, Threads, TikTok or a Mastodon server you turn it on for,
  and a window shows where the platform places the account, signs of
  coordination, how the account posts, how the reply argues, and whether a
  fact-checker has reviewed the claim.
- Who it is for: people who read replies and comment threads and want to know
  who is talking before they weigh what is said.
- Try it: download the release for your browser from
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/cmmns/releases/latest and load it
  unpacked; the install page is https://harperz9.github.io/cmmns/install.html .
  The command line runs as `cmmns analyze saved-thread.html` (or
  `node bin/radar.mjs analyze saved-thread.html` from the unzipped release).
- What it does not do: it shows signs and their sources; a sign of coordination
  is evidence to weigh and stops short of judging a person. Firefox removes the
  temporary add-on on restart until a signed build is published.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/cmmns.html ,
  https://harperz9.github.io/cmmns/install.html ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/cmmns
- Recent verified milestones (2026-11-27): cmmns #130 added `cmmns provenance
  verify` for offline Web/AI provenance verification (agent-card.json, llms.txt,
  JSON-LD, prompt-injection 4/4 catches, engine-receipt/1); cmmns #131 published
  the OSI/FSF AGPL-3.0-only funding.json manifest; cmmns #132 shipped Schema.org
  codemeta.json, llms.txt, CITATION.cff, REUSE SPDX metadata, and browser store
  packaging checklists (9/9 CI pass); cmmns #133 (ffb56129, 1,750/1,750 tests,
  9/9 CI pass) shipped lawful public-record CIB RFC 6962 Merkle provenance and
  PII firewall verification (`cmmns provenance cib-verify`, 28/28 bit-exact
  proofs, 5/5 planted fail-closed controls); cmmns #134 (fdebc810) and #135
  (55ff87f3) graduated 9 pure-OSI MIT BuildLang verification kernels.

## Superframe

The core of The Playground.
Version 0.4.0. Licence MIT (OSI-approved; relicensed from MIT via superframe #162); fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
Node 24 or later. The JavaScript engine has no dependencies; the instruments in
`packages/` pin their own Python dependencies, and the native renderer in
`native/` is a separate C++23 build.

- What it does: you describe a piece in plain words; the engine compiles the
  words into a recipe of elements, each a law with weights, and renders it from
  a seed as paint, living type, a line drawing, a material, a sound and a touch
  pattern. Each render writes a study of its own parts: plain sentences and alt
  text for people and screen readers, and structured data for software.
- Who it is for: artists, designers and anyone who reads better through one
  sense than another; left to right in a picture is time in its sound, and top
  to bottom is pitch.
- Try it: `git clone https://github.com/HarperZ9/superframe`, then
  `npm run make -- "heavy rust coral upper left, fine teal frost on the right" out/first --seed first`.
- What it does not do: elements do not act on one another yet, the intent
  reader knows a small English vocabulary, and the type is the weakest
  crossing. It is a creative tool and makes no claims about therapy.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/playground/#superframe ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/superframe
- Recent verified milestones (2026-11-27; published release Superframe 0.4.0, newer items merged on origin/main):
  native/bld/ bit-exact 0-ULP C++23 to BuildLang renderer parity reached 39 of 39 modules;
  superframe #162 relicensed Superframe to the pure OSI MIT License (294f3f3e);
  112/112 pure-OSI MIT BuildLang WASM modules + 600/600 5-backend GPU shaders with live 5-way GLSL FMA parity (#68984);
  superframe #156 shipped clean-room taste synths, Estuary-Space FX rack, Estuary Clock-Drift DAW, and Round 3 studio audio
  (36/36 Welch PSD pass); superframe #157 added CITATION.cff, codemeta.json,
  and llms.txt discovery manifests; superframe #158 shipped the Low Water 5-era
  deterministic coastal civilization, settlement, and tide simulation layer plus
  bit-exact coastal_kernel.bld; RAW DX12 Waves 74-92 pass 96/96 live
  moving-camera Skyrim SE checks and 159/159 RTX 4090 heuristics (CS-040 16 km fog shadow cache, dark_mo=0.001633 all-time best, 0 D3D12 errors).

## EMET

Version 1.3.1. Licence MPL-2.0 for 1.3.1 and earlier; AGPL-3.0-only from the
next release. Python 3.8 or newer, no dependencies. Ports in Rust, Node.js and Go.

- What it does: checks whether a file still matches the SHA-256 you recorded
  for it and answers MATCH, DRIFT or UNVERIFIABLE. It seals a verdict into a
  small JSON receipt that anyone can check on their own machine.
- Who it is for: anyone who has to show that a document, dataset or prompt a
  model, a reviewer or a pipeline read is the same one that was approved.
- Try it: `python -m pip install emet`, then `emet anchor report.md` and
  `emet verify report.md`.
- What it does not do: it compares bytes. It does not judge whether the content
  of a matching file is correct. With no recorded hash it answers UNVERIFIABLE
  and exits 2 without guessing.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/emet.html , https://github.com/HarperZ9/emet ,
  https://pypi.org/project/emet/

## BuildLang

Version 1.15.0 (crates.io Stage-0 Rust bootstrap). Licence AGPL-3.0-only core / MIT libs. Self-hosting compiler written in BuildLang with Stage-2 zero-C 5-ISA self-compilation.

- What it does: a compiled language where a function's type lists its side
  effects, such as file, network and C access, so a call that reads a file
  without declaring it fails to compile. It builds native binaries through C
  and emits HLSL and GLSL shaders; SPIR-V, LLVM IR, WebAssembly and other
  backends are experimental.
- Who it is for: systems and graphics programmers who want the compiler to show
  what a piece of code is allowed to touch.
- Try it: `cargo install buildlang`, then `buildc doctor`.
- What it does not do: the experimental backends are not production paths; the
  C backend is.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/buildlang.html ,
  https://github.com/HarperZ9/buildlang , https://crates.io/crates/buildlang
- Recent verified milestones (2026-11-27): buildlang #344 wired the V5
  certified e-graph superoptimizer into buildc (`--superopt`, `--emit-cert`,
  `buildc verify-cert`); buildlang #346 added certified GPU polyhedral loop
  tiling + uniformity-safe subgroup auto-vectorization (`--emit-gpu-cert` across
  WGSL, HLSL, MSL, SPIR-V); buildlang #345 published the AGPL-3.0-only
  funding.json; buildlang #348 shipped `CITATION.cff`, `codemeta.json`,
  `llms.txt` discovery manifests and fixed `editors/vscode` `vsce` packaging;
  buildlang #349 burned down `universe/CHECK-FAILS.txt` to 150 (126/276
  passing, bddba429); buildlang #350 migrated `universe/`, `suite/`,
  runtime/audio, and FSL registry packages to pure OSI MIT (c3b2e5dd) while
  keeping core `buildc` AGPL-3.0-only; buildlang #351 (14a5260c, 15/15 CI green)
  added certified 2026 SOTA kernel rewrites (-70.5% online-softmax op-cost,
  -42.1% Gated-DeltaNet + block-scaled dot, -33.3% FA4 Horner exp2, plus live
  `buildc 1.15.0 --superopt` dogfooding cutting MIR cost by -70.31% across 265
  certified rewrites with 0.0 drift, #68529) and GPU TV across WGSL, HLSL, MSL,
  and SPIR-V; Stage 2 == Stage 3 self-hosting reached a byte-identical fixed
  point (91,649 B C99, #68483) and Zero-C direct `.wasm` self-hosting emitted
  202-376 B modules passing 5/5 live in Node (#68517); F6 BDB query engine ran
  73.45x faster than sqlite3 on 68,500 rows (500/500 fuzz caught, #68536);
  BuildOS-Core capability microkernel + A/B state + supervisor (#68490/#68504/
  #68509) and clean-room CRE engine triad (207.75M BSA/s, 56.09x PEX AOT, 625x
  draw cut, #68502/#68511/#68520) passed fail-closed; plus native compiled
  benchmarks (Data Forge 283,687.3 rows/s, Articulate 27,606.0 docs/s, INV-01
  194.59 M loops/s, N18 3DGS 323.60 FPS = 1.93x C++23, NTC610 -83.33% 4K PBR
  VRAM), J13 Model Epigenetics (100% weights-only, #68474), buildlang #352
  (ReShade UV fix, Verilog-2001 RTL backend, String::as_bytes fix, 304c4638),
  buildlang #353 (CHECK-FAILS burned down to 135, f83db229), Zero-C 5-target
  quad-arch self-hosting (400.77x Python on x64-elf), 18-module 86.06 KB live
  WASM bench, 485 zero-FLAG verified formula kernels, and 223/234 (95.30%)
  built author ideas enforced via Gate 6.

## raw-native

The native renderer of The Playground, released under the name raw-native.
Version 0.8.0. Licence MIT (OSI-approved; relicensed via superframe #162). C++23; Windows, Linux and WebAssembly, with
optional D3D12 and WebGPU builds.

- What it does: renders a 3D scene on the CPU and computes ambient occlusion two
  ways, with the screen-space shortcut real-time engines use and by ray
  tracing, then writes both images, a per-pixel error map and a JSON
  certificate with a verdict: verified inside the tolerance, refuted outside.
- Who it is for: graphics developers who need a reference to test an occlusion,
  shading or colour implementation against, or renders that come out the same
  on every machine.
- Try it: build from https://github.com/HarperZ9/superframe/tree/main/native and run
  `raw_native_cli --out ./out`.
- What it does not do: the default view comes back refuted (RMSE 0.135 against
  a tolerance of 0.12); the record keeps that result.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/playground/#native , https://github.com/HarperZ9/superframe/tree/main/native

## Telos

Version 0.9.0. Licence MIT (OSI-approved; relicensed from MIT). Node.js 20 or newer, no npm dependencies.

- What it does: a local MCP server and command line for AI agents. It lets an
  agent read web pages and public APIs, triage a failed GitHub Actions run,
  check an HTML page for accessibility and size problems, and drive a browser
  or Windows apps after you grant access. Gated actions go to a hash-chained log.
- Who it is for: people running agents in MCP hosts such as Claude Code, Codex
  or the OpenAI Agents SDK who want those agents to act with a record.
- Try it: `npx -y project-telos-mcp` in an MCP host config. A `tools/list` call
  against 0.9.0 returns 50 tools.
- What it does not do: nothing that controls a browser or app runs until you
  issue a grant. Install it as `project-telos-mcp`; the npm name `telos`
  belongs to an unrelated package.
- Links: https://github.com/HarperZ9/telos , https://www.npmjs.com/package/project-telos-mcp

## learn

Version 2.3.0. Licence MIT (OSI-approved; relicensed from Fair Source). Node.js 20 or newer, no dependencies.

- What it does: a study planner for the terminal and for agents over MCP. You
  list your objectives and record each practice attempt; it tells you what is
  due for review, which mistakes keep coming back, what order to practise in,
  and whether you have reached mastery.
- Who it is for: anyone studying for a course, an exam or a certification who is
  comfortable in a terminal, and developers who want an agent to plan study
  sessions.
- Try it: `npx -y @harperz9/learn@2.3.0 tutor plan mysession --topic "derivatives" --objectives "power-rule,chain-rule"`.
- What it does not do: it never answers a graded question. Its course engine
  stops at every graded step for you to do yourself.
- Links: https://harperz9.github.io/learn.html , https://github.com/HarperZ9/learn ,
  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@harperz9/learn

## open-archives

Version 0.1.0, not yet released. Licence AGPL-3.0-only. Python 3.11 or newer,
standard library only; media work uses ffmpeg.

- What it does: searches free archives and museum collections with one query,
  from archive.org and Wikimedia Commons to the Met and NASA, downloads the
  items you pick, and cuts clips, audio loops and textures from them. Every
  item carries its licence class and rights basis.
- Who it is for: filmmakers, game and design makers who need period reference
  images, b-roll, sound and textures they can ship.
- Try it: `git clone https://github.com/HarperZ9/superframe`, then run from
  `library/open-archives`:
  `python -m openarchives search "cotton mill" --media image --from 1837 --to 1955`.
- What it does not do: it records the rights basis it finds; a licence you hold
  or a fair-use call is yours to record with `rights`.
- Links: https://github.com/HarperZ9/superframe/tree/main/library/open-archives

## discover

Version 0.1.2. Licence AGPL-3.0-only. Python 3.11 or newer, standard library only.

- What it does: before a release, checks that people can find a project: a
  README that opens with what it does and a command to run, GitHub description
  and topics, package keywords, CITATION.cff, page titles and descriptions,
  JSON-LD, sitemap, robots access for search crawlers, llms.txt, and video
  chapters and hashtags. It scores the result, lists fixes, and with `--gate`
  fails CI.
- Who it is for: maintainers who ship open-source tools, sites or videos and
  want them found by the people they serve.
- Try it: `python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/HarperZ9/discover@v0.1.2"`
  then `discover repo . --gate`.
- What it does not do: it checks form, not merit, and claims no ranking effect.
  Its video check fails engagement bait.
- Links: https://github.com/HarperZ9/flywheel/tree/main/packages/discover

repositories under HarperZ9 (0 private exposed).
